title: Integration
overview: Use integration by parts, substitution and partial fractions to integrate a wider range of functions, including trig integrals. This guide turns the current syllabus outcomes into a connected revision sequence: learn the ideas, practise the method, then use the recall cards and checklist to diagnose what still needs work.
syllabusPoints: Integrate exponential, logarithmic and trigonometric forms using reverse differentiation.
Use substitution, integration by parts and partial fractions.
Evaluate definite integrals and recognise when bounds must change.
Select and combine techniques for unfamiliar integrands.

definitions.definition: Replacing an expression by a new variable to simplify an integral.
A product-rule rearrangement used to integrate products.
A signed accumulated quantity evaluated between fixed limits.
A decomposition that turns a rational expression into simpler integrable terms.
The arbitrary constant required for an indefinite integral.

sections.title: Standard reverse derivatives
content: Recognise ∫f′(x)/f(x) dx=ln|f(x)|+C and ∫eᵃˣ⁺ᵇ dx=eᵃˣ⁺ᵇ/a+C. Similarly account for the inner derivative in sin(ax+b), cos(ax+b) and sec²(ax+b).
bullets: Use ln|f(x)| unless the domain guarantees f(x)>0.
Differentiate the result mentally to check the scale factor.

sections.title: Substitution
content: Choose u for the repeated inner expression, calculate du, and rewrite every x and dx term. For definite integrals either change both limits to u-values or return fully to x before applying the original limits.
bullets: A substitution is incomplete if x remains in the new integrand.
Write new bounds beside u=… to avoid mixing variables.

sections.title: Integration by parts
content: Use ∫u(dv/dx)dx=uv−∫v(du/dx)dx. Choose u so it becomes simpler when differentiated—commonly logarithmic or algebraic before trig/exponential. Repeated use may be needed.
bullets: Keep brackets around the second integral to protect the minus sign.

sections.title: Partial fractions and trig identities
content: Decompose rational functions before integrating; repeated linear terms lead to powers such as (ax+b)⁻². For sin²x or cos²x use double-angle identities. Some integrals need a sequence: algebraic division, partial fractions, then standard forms.
bullets: A 1/(x²+a²) term integrates to an arctangent form.
Simplify the integrand before choosing a method.

examTips: Include +C for every indefinite integral, but not for a definite value.
After a difficult integral, differentiate your antiderivative to verify it.
Show the mathematical setup and exact working before the final rounded answer; unsupported calculator output may not earn method marks.
commonMistakes: Using old x-limits after changing the variable to u.
Missing the inner derivative scale factor.
Applying integration by parts when a simple substitution is available.

quickRecall.question: When should limits be changed in substitution?
quickRecall.answer: When the integral is rewritten in the new variable; otherwise return completely to x before using x-limits.

quickRecall.question: What is a strong choice for u in ∫x eˣ dx?
quickRecall.answer: Choose u=x because differentiation simplifies it, and integrate eˣ as dv/dx.

quickRecall.question: Which pattern gives a logarithm?
quickRecall.answer: An integrand of the form f′(x)/f(x).
